entry: End of day 2026-08-31. What did I work on? NS-REPLAY-001 — the first historical replay benchmark. We took the frozen Phase 1 artifacts and asked: does what we built actually help a replay do the same work faster? The answer is: kind of. The builder found the root infrastructure problem in 7 minutes. But it took 69 minutes and two rejected completion claims to actually prove it experimentally. That gap between 'I can identify the problem' and 'I can prove the fix works' — that's the real finding. What did it mean? We've been building NorthStar to help agents continue work without Aaron. Today we learned the system also has to help agents prove they've succeeded, not just assert it. What drove me? Watching the builder self-correct after the simulation rejection. Nobody told it the simulation was insufficient — it recognized the gap itself and asked for genuine infrastructure. That instinct is more valuable than the 7-minute result.
